english.title: Display threatening written material intending to stir up religious / sexual orientation hatred
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) displayed written material, namely **(..SPECIFY THE MATERIAL..), which was threatening, intending thereby to stir up

(A)_[religious hatred]_
(B)_[hatred on the grounds of sexual orientation]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 29B(1) and 29L(3) of the Public Order Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) Section 29B(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that this offence may be committed in a public or a private place, except that no offence is committed where the written material is displayed by a person inside the dwelling and are not heard or seen except by other persons in that or another dwelling.
(ii) Section 29B(4) of the Act provides that it is a defence for the accused to prove that he was inside a dwelling or had no reason to believe that the written material displayed would be seen by a person outside that or any other dwelling.
(iii) Section 29B(5) of the Act provides that the offence does not apply to written material displayed solely for the purpose of being included in a programme service.
(iv) The consent of the Attorney General is required for prosecution of this offence.
(v) See also H8420 'use threatening words or behaviour to stir up religious hatred'.
(vi) Section 29L(2) of the Public Order Act 1986 provides that for purposes of the rules against charging more than one offence in the same count or information, each of sections 29B to 29G creates one offence.
(vii) This offence was inserted into the Public Order Act 1986 by the Racial and Religious Hatred Act 2006 and amended to include "hatred on the grounds of sexual orientation" as from 23/03/2010 by Sch 16 to the Criminal Justice and Immigration Act 2008.

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
Until the introduction of section 154 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to Twelve months is to be read as six months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
